definitions.explanation: Describes something so minor or unimportant that it does not merit attention or discussion. Literally 'not sufficient to take up.'

examples.japanese: {取|と}るに{足|た}らない⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧だ。
⟦そんな→そんな：01645_sonna⟧{取|と}るに{足|た}らないこと⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{悩|なや}む→悩む：02380_nayamu⟧な。
examples.english: Don't worry about something so insignificant.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{取|と}るに{足|た}らない⟦{人物|じんぶつ}→人物：03356_jinbutsu⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}われていた→思う：00492_omou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、のち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{功績|こうせき}→功績：04143_kouseki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{残|のこ}した→残す：01975_nokosu⟧。
examples.english: He was considered an insignificant person, but later left behind great achievements.

notes:
A literary expression meaning "not worth taking up" or "not worth considering." Has an elevated, slightly formal tone and is commonly encountered in writing, speeches, and formal conversation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Composed of ⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ (to take) + ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (particle) + ⟦{足|た}らない→足る：03914_taru⟧ (not sufficient). The underlying meaning is "not sufficient to be taken up [for discussion/attention]."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {取|と}るに{足|た}らない⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧: a trivial problem
- {取|と}るに{足|た}らない⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧: a trivial matter
- {取|と}るに{足|た}らない⟦{存在|そんざい}→存在：03326_sonzai⟧: an insignificant existence
- {取|と}るに{足|た}らない⟦{人物|じんぶつ}→人物：03356_jinbutsu⟧: an insignificant person

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦くだらない→くだらない：09416_kudaranai⟧: worthless; stupid — more colloquial and dismissive, often expressing contempt. {取|と}るに{足|た}らない is more measured and literary.
- たいしたことない: no big deal — casual and reassuring. {取|と}るに{足|た}らない is more formal and definitive.
- ⟦つまらない→つまらない：00590_tsumaranai⟧: boring; trivial — broader in meaning; can mean "boring" or "worthless." {取|と}るに{足|た}らない specifically means "not worth considering."
